small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose now dominates runtime (fast_p only 1.39 with the fused GELU+GN already efficient). Further tuning of BLOCK/num_warps in the norm kernel will not move the needle — focus must shift to the conv.
- If staying in-kernel: try persistent kernel over the group (keep accumulators in registers across the two passes by tiling HW into fewer/larger chunks), and consider Welford for numerical stability with single pass.
- Pre-broadcast weight/bias loads outside the inner HW loop by loading per-channel scalars once (since GROUP_SIZE=8 channels × HW=65536, iterating per channel is cheaper than gathering with c_in_group indexing every iter).
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton kernel. For stride=1, kernel=3, ConvTranspose2d is equivalent to a regular Conv2d with the weight flipped and padding=2 (full conv). Implement as a tiled GEMM (im2col-style implicit gather): one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) with BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 sweeping, channels-last layout for coalesced K-dim loads.
- Fuse the GELU + GroupNorm first-pass reduction into the conv kernel's epilogue is hard (GN reduces across all spatial), but at least fuse the GELU + the partial sum/sum_sq accumulation per (N, group) into the conv epilogue by writing GELU output and accumulating stats via atomics into per-group buffers, then a tiny second kernel applies the normalization. This eliminates one full read of the post-conv tensor.
- Alternative: since out_channels=64, num_groups=8, GROUP_SIZE=8, HW=65536, the GN reduction is huge per group (~524K elements). A persistent conv kernel that produces output channels-last and writes contiguous (N, group) tiles enables the GN kernel to stream input once. Prioritize layout choice (NHWC) end-to-end.
